correctness.rationale: For all characteristic-two k and n >=5, a nonzero linear wedge-annihilator forces f=v wedge omega. Alternating rank gives canonical strata; the annihilator is three-space at rank two and exactly a line at higher rank. Wedge multiplication reduces to the tensor product of s four-dimensional two-generator complexes. Its homology Hilbert series yields the complete graded ranks by a direct rank identity; a Gaussian/GL-Sp fiber count gives all q-power-of-two populations, and a projective incidence vector bundle proves irreducibility and dimensions. Direct stand-alone F2 monomial multiplication exhausts 2^20 six-dimensional cubics and checks canonical graded profiles through dimension eight; those experiments corroborate, and do not replace, the general proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed all-dimension result concerns precisely cubics with a nonzero degree-one wedge annihilator, their complete graded exterior-multiplication ranks, dimension/geometry, and finite-field alternating-rank populations. Earlier six-dimensional orbit results imply the n=6 F2 census, which is not asserted to be historically new. Primary full texts examined address divided-power and symplectic-contraction differentials, six-dimensional trivector orbits, or Grassmannian-hyperplane representatives, not the uniform conditional rank, point-count and geometry theorem; published-finding corpus searches did not identify the same implications. value.rationale: A natural rank-jump condition for cubic elements in exterior algebras singles out the closed divisibility locus. The theorem provides its complete all-n characteristic-two orbit classification, graded exterior multiplication ranks, irreducible geometry and exact finite-field populations, refining basic triviality/nontriviality and giving meaningful structural information even when arbitrary cubics in larger dimension remain unclassified. The result is an infinite-family structural census, not a textbook scalar substitution or small-case table.
